title: RHom base change for a perfect complex
statement: Let A\to A' be a morphism of commutative rings. Regard complexes of A-modules (resp. A'-modules) as complexes of modules over the ringed site with one object and ring A (resp. A'), so that RHom_A, RHom_{A'} denote the derived Hom of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] for these ringed sites and A'\otimes_A^L- the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], computed by K-flat resolutions. Let E be a perfect complex of A-modules, i.e. E is isomorphic in D(A) to a bounded complex of finite projective A-modules (equivalently \widetilde E is perfect on Spec(A) in the sense of [def-pc-perfect-complex], by [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective]), and let K be any complex of A-modules. The canonical map A'\otimes_A^L RHom_A(E,K)\to RHom_{A'}(A'\otimes_A^L E,A'\otimes_A^L K), namely the A'-linear extension of the A-linear map RHom_A(E,K)\to RHom_{A'}(A'\otimes_A^L E,A'\otimes_A^L K) induced by the functor A'\otimes_A^L-, is an isomorphism in D(A').

proof.text: The model m already supplies the bounded finite-projective source P, K-flat target Q, representative isomorphisms, extended-source boundedness and projectivity, and source and target derived counit isomorphisms. ringRHomModelIso identifies both RHom expressions with their ordinary Hom models. The model-identification factors in perfectRHomBaseChangeMap are isomorphisms, as are the product-category representative maps and their functor images.

proof.text: Apply perfectRingHom_scalarExtension_isIso to P=m.source and Q=m.target, with m.bounded, m.projective and m.finite. This makes d.homMap P Q invertible and hence its image under DerivedCategory.Q invertible.

proof.text: Apply perfectRingHom_isKFlat to the same P,Q and m.target_kFlat. The field d.counit_kFlat makes the counit on Hom(P,Q) invertible. The quotient factorization maps in ringDerivedExtensionCounit are images of isomorphisms, so their composite with this counit is also invertible.

source.place: Lemma 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1); bounded finite-projective representative argument

proof.text: Unfold perfectRHomBaseChangeMap. All six factors are now isomorphisms: the source representative change, the source RHom model identification, the derived extension counit on Hom, Q of the normalized Hom-complex map, the inverse target RHom model identification, and the target representative change. Compose their inverses in reverse order, as supplied by the categorical IsIso composition instance. This proves the unchanged conclusion.
